scope: Local recovery regression history; no production incident or enterprise readiness claim

observations.check: Authenticated container regression after database TCP outage
observations.evidence: Timed out: database restored and supervisor replacement ready
observations.lesson: The single replacement attempt lacked process diagnostics. Cause of the initial timeout remains unconfirmed; do not call this a demonstrated production fix.

observations.check: Diagnostic rerun with private process-output capture
observations.evidence: Original readiness, service/database SIGKILL, orchestration archive restore and two-effect checks passed with the same limits.

observations.check: Injected database-down replacement startup in authenticated containers
observations.evidence: docker kill returned container is not running while its CLI child exit was still propagating
observations.lesson: The proof must accept already-stopped/removing containers only after the actual child exit is observed within the unchanged shutdown deadline. Other Docker errors must still fail.
Both actual initial replacements terminate with the database still unavailable; each next process recovers once connectivity returns. Readiness and child-exit deadlines are unchanged.

remaining: Remote deployed supervisor behavior, dependency availability and reliability under repeated faults require separate acceptance. A passing rerun alone does not establish availability.
